## Connecting Symbolic Equations, `lme4` Formulas, and APA Outputs

Multilevel models are taught and reviewed in level-by-level Raudenbush & Bryk
notation ($\beta_{qj}$, $\gamma_{qs}$, $u_{qj}$, $r_{ij}$), yet estimated in R
through mixed-model formulas. `mlmr` keeps both representations synchronized
both **before** and **after** estimation.

## Live Pre-Fit Symbolic Equations (`mlm_spec_equations()`)

Analysts can verify their Level-1, Level-2, and Level-3 equations while
specifying the model—before pressing Fit. `mlm_spec_equations()` inspects an
`mlm_spec` object and dataset to produce publication-grade symbolic LaTeX
equations, plain-language level notes, combined mixed-model equations, and
$\mathbf{T}$ covariance matrices without fitting the model:

```{r prefit-equations, eval = TRUE}
library(mlmr)

dat <- example_hsb(n_schools = 12, min_students = 10, max_students = 14)
spec <- mlm_spec(
  outcome = "mathscore",
  fixed = list(
    ses = list(center = "CWC"),
    meanses = list(center = "GMC"),
    sector = list(center = "none")
  ),
  grouping = list(schoolid = "schoolid"),
  random = list(schoolid = list(
    intercept = TRUE, slopes = "ses", correlation = TRUE
  )),
  interactions = list(c("ses", "sector")),
  data = dat
)

pre_eq <- mlm_spec_equations(spec)
pre_eq$level
writeLines(strsplit(pre_eq$equations[[2]], "\\\\ ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
```

## Post-Fit Equations and Coefficient Key (`mlm_latex_equations()`)

Once fitted, `mlm_latex_equations()` pairs the symbolic equations with a
complete **Coefficient Key** mapping every hierarchical symbol ($\gamma_{00}$,
$\gamma_{10}$, $\gamma_{11}$, …) to its `lme4` fixed-effect name, numeric
estimate, and random-slope role:

```{r postfit-equations, eval = TRUE}
result <- suppressWarnings(mlm_fit(spec))
eq <- mlm_latex_equations(result)
eq$key
```

## Robust Inference, Variance Tests, and APA Reporting

Beyond standard `lme4` Wald/Satterthwaite/Kenward-Roger fixed-effects tables
(`mlm_apa_tables()`), `mlmr` provides comprehensive multilevel inferential and
diagnostic tables:

```{r reporting-helpers, eval = TRUE}
# Marginal and conditional R^2 (Nakagawa, Johnson, & Schielzeth, 2017)
mlm_r2(result)

# Empirical Bayes reliabilities (lambda) for random intercepts AND slopes
mlm_reliability(result)

# Huber-White cluster-robust sandwich standard errors (CR1 and CR0)
mlm_robust_se(result)

# Multiparameter joint Wald test (e.g., testing sector main + slope moderation)
mlm_wald_test(result, terms = c("sectorPublic", "ses_CWC:sectorPublic"))

# Single-term random-effect LRT chi-square and boundary mixture p-values
mlm_variance_tests(result)

# Bartlett H test of Level-1 residual variance homogeneity across clusters
mlm_homogeneity_test(result)
```

When `lmerTest` is installed, passing `df_method = "satterthwaite"` (or
`"kenward-roger"` with `pbkrtest`) adds denominator degrees of freedom and
$t$-based confidence intervals to Gaussian APA tables.

## Residual Files and Publication Bundle Archive

`mlm_residual_files()` extracts complete-case Level-1 residuals and
cluster-level empirical Bayes estimates with posterior standard errors.
`mlm_write_publication_bundle()` packages the Quarto report (`.qmd`),
standalone reproducible R script (`.R`), raw LaTeX (`amsmath` + `graphicx`),
Word/HTML APA tables, Level-1 and cluster residual CSVs, reproducibility
checklist CSV, and software citation table into a single `.zip` archive:

```{r bundle-example, eval = FALSE}
mlm_write_publication_bundle(result, "mlmr_publication_bundle.zip")
```

Software citations can also be generated directly:

```{r software, eval = TRUE}
mlm_software_apa()
```
